_comment: Scrub rules of tools/story_capture.py. A rule is a regex over one line; `exclude` (full-match) lets a hit through. Non-ASCII letters are written as \u escapes so this file stays ASCII.

rules.why: experiment names built from internal ticket numbers (experiments/measurers)
names of people (FK-11), latin and Cyrillic spellings
the internal GitLab project id and API
the old marketplace name (lives in the internal release repo)
any other Jira-like key; the forge's own prefixes and the stand's synthetic prefixes (LOCAL, CART, TS, OB) are excluded; L126-128 is a source line range, REF-n is the rewrite placeholder

derived._comment: Classes built from the SOURCE root, never from a list of names: the capture reads the values out of the run (person fields, mail addresses, user objects, home folders, the project keys of rewritten tickets), rewrites them to the marks below everywhere, and refuses if any is left in the result. Only FIELD NAMES, marks and the not-a-person words live here.

handle_url.why: a person's (or organisation's) handle inside a public repository URL, with or without scheme, in any of these forms: github.com or gitlab.com (www too) /<handle>, .../users|orgs|sponsors/<handle>, api.<host>/repos|users|orgs/<handle>, raw.githubusercontent.com/<handle>, the scp form git@<host>:<handle>/..., and <handle>.github.io; the slash may be /, %2F (percent-encoded) or a backslash-slash pair (JSON-escaped text). The handle is followed by / or .git or the end of the token: it becomes person-<n> with the number the person map gives it (a collected login with the same spelling keeps its number); the repository name after the handle stays, the host stays. No min length: it is rewritten only inside such a URL

residue_detectors.why: INDEPENDENT of the rewrite pattern (it proves absence, not only a fixpoint): any github.com / gitlab.com host (any subdomain) followed, in the same token and through any slash form or a colon, by a path segment that is not person-<n> (a structural word users/orgs/sponsors/repos alone is allowed)
raw.githubusercontent.com (any subdomain) followed by a path segment that is not person-<n>
the label before .github.io (a pages host) that is not person-<n>, whatever precedes it
any `.claude` + `projects` + a following segment (any case, any slash form, JSON-escaped or percent-encoded) that is not the neutral constant

rewrites.why: corporate URLs (the example rule) in comments and text: a placeholder host, numbered by first appearance; the `/browse/<KEY>` tail stays (the ticket-key row then gives the key the same REF-n as everywhere else, so a key read from the URL still matches), the query is dropped
a bare host under the example.com domain (any subdomain, no scheme; a mail domain too): a neutral host, the same host always the same mark
the Java-style package prefix of the company in package-written text
every match of the jira-tp3 and jira-key rules that is not the story's own task key and not a synthetic stand prefix: one REF number per distinct key, the same in every file

the dash-encoded path of an agent project folder (`.claude/projects/<encoded path>`; `.claude` in any case; backslash, doubled backslash, slash or JSON-escaped slash form; the Windows encoding `C--...` and the POSIX encoding `-home-<user>-...`): it names this machine's layout and the stand folder; a neutral constant. `residue: true` = the residue scan also looks for what this row would still rewrite
the bare product word (the testproject1 rule) in package-written text
